transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It's nice to meet you, too. Thanks for seeing me. Um, well, I guess what brought me in is... well, it's probably not a huge deal, but people keep telling me I'm not listening. Like, my supervisor at the plant, or my wife, they'll be talking right to me, and... I don't know, a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of what they said. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, which I know is annoying. I try really hard to pay attention, I promise, it's just... I don't know, does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Do you ever have trouble hearing what people say, even when you’re trying to listen?

Oh, no, I don't think it's my ears. Like, my hearing itself is fine. We actually have to do those hearing tests at the plant every year and I always pass them, so... I don't want you to think I'm going deaf or anything. It's more just... the words go in, but my brain just sort of drops them? I really do try to be a good listener, I swear, I just... I don't know, I hope I'm explaining that right. Is that what you meant?
Did you have this same kind of trouble paying attention when you were a child?

Yeah, um... I guess it goes back pretty far. I was kind of like this even as a little kid. Though back then, it was more about... well, I wasn't a bad kid, I promise, I just had a lot of energy. 

Like, before I hit middle school, my teachers were always having to move my seat around the classroom because I just couldn't really stay put. And I'd get a little too eager and just call out the answers without raising my hand, or I'd sort of accidentally butt into what the other kids were working on. I got in a little bit of trouble for it back then, but I swear I didn't mean to be disruptive, I just... I couldn't help myself sometimes. 

Is that... does that answer your question? I really hope I don't sound like I was a terrible student or anything.
Do you still feel unusually restless as an adult?

Um, yeah, I guess I do still get kind of restless. I mean, not like I'm running around the plant floor or anything—I'm a hard worker, I really am, and I stay at my station. But, um... if I have to just sit still for too long, like in a meeting or if we're waiting for parts to come down the line, I get this... it's hard to describe. 

It's almost like this pressure just starts building up, you know? Like right in my chest and down in my legs. It just feels like I have to move or do something right that second, or I'm going to just... I don't know, crawl out of my skin. I try to hide it, like I'll just bounce my leg a little or find something to fiddle with so I don't bother anyone. I hope that doesn't sound too weird. Is it normal to feel like that?
Do you often feel worried or on edge, even when there isn’t an obvious reason?

Um, worried? No, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm a particularly anxious guy or anything. I try to just take things as they come, you know? 

Like, sure, if something big happens at work or if bills are tight, I'll get stressed just like anybody else. But I don't just sit around feeling on edge for no reason. I really try to keep a positive attitude. I hope that's okay, that I don't have that... I'm not trying to be difficult or anything, I just honestly don't feel worried like that. Is that a good thing?
Do these attention problems cause trouble for you at work?

Um... well... I really want to say no, because I try so hard to be a good employee. I really do. But... yeah, I guess it has. 

Actually, it's... it's gotten pretty serious. I'm a little embarrassed to admit this, but I've actually had some formal warnings lately. I just get a little too antsy or I lose track of what I'm doing, and on a production line, you know, that's... well, it's not great. I worry all the time that I might accidentally cause a safety problem, or... or even lose my job. I swear I'm not doing it on purpose, I just really struggle to keep it together sometimes. I don't want to be a liability, you know? 

And, um, it's kind of the same at home, too, to be honest. I want to help out, but my wife and kids get pretty frustrated with me. I guess I just end up disrupting our routines instead of actually helping things run smoothly like a good husband and dad should. I feel terrible about it. 

Does that... I mean, is it okay that I'm telling you all this? I really hope you don't think I'm just a careless guy or a bad worker. I'm really trying my best.
